Ben —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement had a quick follow-up about the billing shape before we can issue a formal PO. Two items: 1) Our ERP requires line-level SKU mapping on the PO and we typically request that vendors allow invoice splitting so each SKU can be billed on its own schedule; 2) We need clarity on how volume-tier discounts apply when we split invoices across entities/months — does the discount aggregate to the PO or to each invoice?

I attached our PO template (Medisys_PO_Template.xlsx). Can Redwood accept a PO where each invoice references the same PO ID but different SKU lines are invoiced separately? Also, we prefer consolidated monthly statements for payment run purposes; would that still allow you to honor the volume-tier pricing?

Appreciate any examples of final invoice payloads or required PO fields so we can pass them to AP.

Hi Laura —

Thanks for the clear ask and the PO template — that helps. Short answers up front: yes, we can accept a single PO ID and support per-SKU invoicing (each invoice references the PO and includes the SKU line items you specify). Volume-tier discounts are applied at the PO level (aggregate usage across invoices referencing that PO) rather than per-invoice, so splitting invoices won’t penalize you for tiers.

Two implementation notes: 1) we need the PO_ID to appear in the invoice header and in the invoice XML/CSV line item mapping so our AP team can auto-reconcile; 2) for aggregated tiering we require a monthly reconciliation record when billing crosses tiers — that can be a simple CSV that lists token/usage by SKU for the PO. We can generate that on our side or accept your preferred format.

I’ll loop in Vanessa from Partner Ops for any commercial guardrails and Marissa from Finance for PO acceptance rules.

Next steps: Ben (me) to share a sample invoice and our preferred PO field list; Vanessa to confirm discount cap language; Marissa to confirm any net-term implications if Medisys consolidates to a monthly statement.

Regards,
Ben Carter

Ben/Team —

Thanks for the outline, Ben. A few commercial clarifications from our side so procurement has the right expectations: 
- We can confirm aggregate tiering at the PO level, but discount caps apply per deal (DEAL-4812). If Medisys expects to hit higher volume tiers, we need to lock tier thresholds in the contract (I recommend inserting an appendix with the tier schedule).
- If invoices are split across legal entities or BU codes, we need a single reconciliation doc weekly or monthly (we prefer monthly) to calculate final tier credit/refund adjustments. That doc is used for retrospective crediting; without it, we can only apply tiers on forward billing.
- Net terms: standard is Net 45 for enterprise customers on dedicated capacity. If Medisys consolidates invoices into a single monthly statement, our finance team will still require line-level invoice files for matching. Consolidated statement is fine, but payment will be applied against the oldest outstanding invoice(s) per our aging policy.

Ben — please share the sample invoice (PDF/XML) and PO field list. Laura — if your AP system can accept our sample reconciliation CSV, that will speed acceptance.

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Partner Operations | Redwood Inference
